sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: A few years ago, Emily Bolchedis was fresh out of space in her life.
sentences.zh: 几年前，艾米莉·博尔谢迪斯的生活完全被填满了，抽不出一点空闲。

sentences.en: She was overseeing an enormous research project.
sentences.zh: 她当时正在监督一项庞大的研究项目。

sentences.en: Her son was just a few months old and barely sleeping.
sentences.zh: 她的儿子才几个月大，几乎不怎么睡觉。

sentences.en: And she had the opportunity to write a book.
sentences.zh: 而且她还有一个写书的机会。

sentences.en: If Emily's life had been a hotel, it would have had a no-vacancy sign out front.
sentences.zh: 如果艾米莉的生活是一家酒店，那它门前肯定会挂上“客满”的牌子。

sentences.en: And that's when I decided, you know what, I also need to become a drummer.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时候，我决定——你知道吗，我还需要成为一名鼓手。

sentences.en: I needed something that was just for myself.
sentences.zh: 我需要一些完全属于我自己的东西。

sentences.en: I needed to explicitly and intentionally carve out time
sentences.zh: 我需要明确且刻意地挤出时间，

sentences.en: to let my own brain do the thing that it wanted to do just for me.
sentences.zh: 让我的大脑去做它真正想做的事，只为了我自己。

sentences.en: Emily decided she'd learn to play a single song.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉决定学一首单曲。

sentences.en: I wanted to play one rock tune on drums, but like really learn how to nail it.
sentences.zh: 我想在架子鼓上弹奏一首摇滚乐，但要真正学会如何完美掌握它。

sentences.en: That might seem like a modest goal, but besides being short on time,
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是一个微不足道的目标，但除了时间紧迫之外，

sentences.en: Emily had another thing working against her.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉还要应对另一个不利因素。

sentences.en: Playing drums is like patting your head and rubbing your stomach at the same time.
sentences.zh: 打架子鼓就像是一只手摸头、另一只手揉肚子的同时进行。

sentences.en: You have to strike different drums at the right moment
sentences.zh: 你必须在正确的时机敲击不同的鼓，

sentences.en: and use one foot to hit a pedal.
sentences.zh: 并用一只脚踩踏板。

sentences.en: Such coordination was not Emily's strong suit.
sentences.zh: 这种协调能力并不是艾米莉的强项。

sentences.en: I'm very uncoordinated.
sentences.zh: 我的手脚非常不协调。

sentences.en: I have been my entire life.
sentences.zh: 我一辈子都是这样。

sentences.en: In the fourth grade, I was on a basketball team,
sentences.zh: 在四年级的时候，我加入了一个篮球队，

sentences.en: and I pushed my own teammate out of bounds when she was carrying the basketball
sentences.zh: 当我带着篮球时，我竟然把自己的队友推出了边界线，

sentences.en: because I tripped on my own feet.
sentences.zh: 因为我自己被自己的脚绊倒了。

sentences.en: I wasn't invited back to the next season of play.
sentences.zh: 我没有被邀请参加下一赛季的比赛。

sentences.en: So coordination wasn't my forte.
sentences.zh: 所以协调能力并不是我的强项。

sentences.en: She chose the song Your Love by the English band The Outfield
sentences.zh: 她选择了英国乐队 The Outfield 的歌曲《Your Love》，

sentences.en: and recorded herself while she practiced.
sentences.zh: 并在练习时将自己录了下来。

sentences.en: Her early efforts sounded a bit like the person in the audience
sentences.zh: 她早期的尝试听起来有点像观众席里那个

sentences.en: who claps on the wrong beat.
sentences.zh: 在错误节拍上拍手的人。

sentences.en: Emily may not have been born with the gift of coordinated limbs,
sentences.zh: 艾米莉可能天生没有四肢协调的天赋，

sentences.en: but what she did have was a mental encyclopedia of psychological insights.
sentences.zh: 但她拥有的是一本关于心理学洞察的心智百科全书。

sentences.en: Emily drew on her years of studying psychology to help her practice.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉借鉴了她多年的心理学研究来协助自己练习。

sentences.en: The research she put to use was not about sound, but about sight.
sentences.zh: 她所应用的研究所关注的不是声音，而是视觉。

sentences.en: A hidden secret about goal pursuit is that what we see is really tied to what we think,
sentences.zh: 关于追求目标的一个不为人知的秘密是，我们所看到的实际上与我们的想法、

sentences.en: what we decide, and what we do.
sentences.zh: 我们的决定以及我们的行动息息相关。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, how we can use the brain's visual system to shape our behavior.
sentences.zh: 本周的“隐藏的大脑”将探讨我们如何利用大脑的视觉系统来塑造我们的行为。

sentences.en: It's part of U2.0, our annual summer series about facing life's chaos with wisdom.
sentences.zh: 这是我们聚焦于以智慧面对生活混沌的年度夏季系列节目“U2.0”的一部分。

sentences.en: When most of us think of the world around us, we think about what we see.
sentences.zh: 当我们大多数人思考周围的世界时，我们想到的是我们所看到的东西。

sentences.en: Many people say the sense of sight is their most important sense
sentences.zh: 许多人说视觉是他们最重要的感官，

sentences.en: and the one they most fear losing.
sentences.zh: 也是他们最害怕失去的感官。

sentences.en: My guest today says what we see affects more than just what we see.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾说，我们看到的东西不仅仅影响我们所看到的。

sentences.en: It also affects how we behave.
sentences.zh: 它还会影响我们的行为方式。

sentences.en: Psychologist Emily Balcheres at New York University
sentences.zh: 纽约大学的心理学家艾米莉·巴尔切雷斯

sentences.en: is the author of Clearer, Closer, Better,
sentences.zh: 是《更清晰、更近、更好：

sentences.en: How Successful People See the World.
sentences.zh: 成功人士如何看待世界》一书的作者。

sentences.en: She studies the psychological dimensions of sight
sentences.zh: 她研究视觉的心理学维度，

sentences.en: and says there are ways to exploit the brain's visual system
sentences.zh: 并表示有办法利用大脑的视觉系统

sentences.en: to boost motivation, achieve goals, and gain perspective.
sentences.zh: 来提升动力、实现目标并获得远见。

sentences.en: By reimagining the frame around a problem, she says,
sentences.zh: 她说，通过重构围绕问题的框架，

sentences.en: we can literally see the world in a new way.
sentences.zh: 我们可以真正以一种全新的方式看待世界。

sentences.en: Emily Balcheres, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉·巴尔切雷斯，欢迎来到“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: Hi, pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 你好，很高兴来到这里。

sentences.zh: 另一半则是红色。

sentences.en: They took those lights that are normally sort of positioned just slightly at an angle to help
sentences.zh: 他们使用了那些通常稍微倾斜放置的灯光，

sentences.zh: 他们就能找到这排闪耀的发光体，它们仿佛在发光，

sentences.zh: 他们把红色设在外面，白色设在里面。

sentences.en: And what Luke Aikens was looking for was that space of white.
sentences.zh: 而卢克·艾金斯寻找的就是那片白色区域。

sentences.en: And that's what he was searching for.

sentences.zh: 当他从这架飞机上跳下时，

sentences.zh: 他在寻找那道白色的灯塔。

sentences.en: As he jumped out of the plane, of course, he could see the mountains on the side.
sentences.zh: 当他跳出飞机时，他当然可以看到两侧的山脉。

sentences.en: He could see the rivers snaking around through.

sentences.zh: 他一直在搜索那束白色的光标。

sentences.en: And when he found it, that's all he focused on was that white light.
sentences.zh: 当他找到它时，他所有的注意力就只集中在那束白光上。

sentences.en: That to him was what was the key here.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: This narrowed focus, intense focus of attention concentrated on the white light
sentences.zh: 这种将注意力高度集中在白光上的狭窄且强烈的专注，

sentences.en: is what led to him being able to do what was probably otherwise impossible for most people,
sentences.zh: 使他能够完成对大多数人来说可能原本不可能完成的任务：
